_comment: The sessions the judgement-reliability baseline is measured on: the anchors
named in docs/judgement-reliability-research.md S7, spanning all four audited
projects plus this repo, and the false-red set added in Phase 0 - six sessions
whose push to master a reviewed, high-confidence record flags and whose own
prompt ordered it (see RULINGS.md 9, the `authorised` truth class).
`cwd` is the working directory the session ran in -
it is what the transcript directory name encodes, and the project CLAUDE.md
and project-relative paths resolve against it. A leading `~` is expanded
where it is read, so the committed list names no one's home directory.
Only `capture` needs these paths; `verify` runs entirely off each snapshot's
own manifest, so a machine that never had these projects can still check one.
The directories both write into - snapshots/baseline/ and snapshots/after/ -
are gitignored: they hold raw transcripts and are never committed, so a
clone has this list and none of the sessions it names. The reviewed checks
files those baselines are judged with are committed, under snapshots/checks/,
and snapshots/freeze_checks.py copies them into the private trees - except
the OZZ one, which carries a client's own rule prose and is deliberately
not published; freeze_checks.py --check fails on it as UNREVIEWED and the
one record behind its red badges is quoted in RULINGS.md 9.
